description: Enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity focused on latency SLO alignment and reserved GPU planning for a real-time financial chat + reranking workload.
notes:
Summary: Cerulean is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a mission-critical financial assistant (real-time chat + document reranking). Primary ask: precise SLO definitions and measurement methodology so legal/procurement can accept SLA. They have strong data residency and audit requirements; prefer VPC deployment.

Key requirements / targets (customer-provided):
- Workload: low-latency conversational assistant + server-side reranker for search results. Mix: ~65% chat (streaming), 35% batch/rerank (non-streaming).
- Throughput: steady-state 500 req/s with short bursts to 2k req/s.
- Latency targets: non-streaming generation p95 <= 200ms (end-to-end server-side), p99 <= 350ms; streaming token emit p99 <= 300ms per-token after first byte. Client-side (E2E incl. network) p95 <= 250ms for short responses (<=64 tokens).
- Consistency: emphasize p99 for SLAs (financial app, user-facing).
- Availability: 99.95% target uptime for dedicated pool, with clear maintenance windows and fallbacks.

Discussion points on SLO definition/measurement:
- Server-side vs client-side: Cerulean insists SLA state server-side inference latency (time from request entered Redwood edge to last-token-complete on server) but legal wants an E2E example measurement that includes last-mile network — require both metrics documented.
- p50/p95/p99 semantics: must define request population (all requests, only successful responses, streaming-first-byte vs last-byte). They prefer quantiles computed on success-only, with explicit exclusion rules for client cancel/timeout.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: need separate SLO buckets. For streaming: measure per-token emit latency and TTFB (time-to-first-byte); for non-streaming: measure request->final-token latency.
- Measurement windows & outlier handling: suggest rolling 30d window for SLO reporting, 7d for operational alerts. Define outlier policy for infra incidents and GC pauses.
- Synthetic vs production measurement: Cerulean wants Redwood to provide reproducible synthetic benchmarks (workload replay) and an optional client-side SDK to emit identical timing metrics for correlation.

Technical asks for Dedicated sizing and SLA:
- Request Redwood sizing worksheet with conservative reserved GPU count and expected headroom for 2k burst. Preliminary ask: equivalent of 4-6 A100-class GPUs with autoscale guardrail.
- Need explicit throughput guarantees per reservation tier (tokens/sec, requests/sec).
- Fallback behavior: when reserved capacity exhausted, define routing policy (queueing, fallback to smaller model, temporary rate limiting) and how that's reflected in SLA credits.
- Observability: token-level tracing, per-route p50/p95/p99 histograms, and ability to export raw timing to their Splunk.

Timeline & recent activities:
- 2026-01-22: Intro call (AE Sasha + SE Diego) — scope & compliance kickoff (FF-2026-01-22).
- 2026-02-11: Deep dive SLO discussion (SE-led). Request for explicit streaming p99 definition logged (FF-2026-02-11-cerulean-1).
- 2026-02-25: Legal sent preliminary security questionnaire; Redwood provided SOC2 artifact link.
- 2026-03-02: SLA negotiation call — Cerulean pushing for 99.95% and clear penalty matrix (FF-2026-03-02-cerulean-slo-review).
- 2026-03-08: Internal engineering asks for a 48h traffic replay with their telemetry for p99 validation.

Quotes & call snippets:
- "We can accept server-side SLOs if you give us a reproducible client-side measurement method we can run ourselves." — Cerulean infra lead.
- "Must exclude client cancels from p99 calculation; otherwise numbers are meaningless for us." — Cerulean PM.

Open items / blockers:
- Redwood to provide: 1) dedicated-sizing worksheet, 2) definition doc for p50/p95/p99 including exclusion rules, 3) streaming measurement spec (per-token vs TTFB), 4) sample SLA penalty matrix.
- Legal to finish data residency appendix and confirm retention controls.
- Procurement: budget sign-off for reserved GPU commitment (estimate $150k-$400k ARR).

Next steps agreed:
- Redwood -> send dedicated-sizing worksheet + measurement spec (owner: SE Diego) by 2026-03-12.
- Schedule 48h traffic replay w/ Redwood infra (target window 2026-03-22 to 2026-03-24).
- Draft SLA pull request (Redwood legal) for Cerulean review by 2026-03-18.
